abstract: Eye movement-related eardrum oscillations (EMREOs) are acoustic signals recorded in the ear canal induced by saccades, whose amplitude and time course relate to the saccade vector. While horizontal saccades evoke robust, and largely opposing EMREO signals in the two ears, the reliability and informational content of vertical EMREOs has remained more elusive. Here, we analyzed bilateral EMREOs in human participants performing visually guided horizontal and vertical saccades. Consistent with previous work, horizontal saccades induced stereotyped, opposing waveforms across ears. In contrast, vertical EMREOs exhibited distinct temporal profiles between upward and downward directions, weaker signal modulation, and substantially higher inter-individual variability, particularly for downward saccades. To quantify the parametric information carried by single-trial bilateral EMREOs about the saccade vector, we applied multivariate classification and reconstruction analyses. The cardinal saccade direction was classified above chance, with significantly higher accuracy for horizontal than vertical saccades. Similarly, the reconstruction recovered horizontal saccade components more accurately than vertical ones, yet severely underestimated saccade amplitudes with high variability. These findings demonstrate that EMREOs carry reliable categorical saccade information, but primarily along the horizontal axis, and provide only weak and noisy parametric estimates of the full two-dimensional saccade vector. They also suggest that EMREOs may be particularly driven by the differential engagement of oculomotor neuromuscular pathways across the two sides of the brainstem.
